additions.definition: A rigid, handled blade used to divide dough and clear a work surface. Its straight edge is suited to working on a bench; it is distinct from a flexible bowl scraper.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A flexible scraper that follows the inside of a bowl to gather sticky dough or mixture. It need not have the rigid blade or handle of a bench scraper.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A tool that makes repeated impressions or perforations in dough to limit unwanted puffing. It performs docking; a pastry wheel instead cuts along a line.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A device for tracking a cooking or preparation interval, whether separate or built into an appliance. Elapsed time is a cue to check the food, not a measurement of its temperature.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A broad, handled tool for supporting and moving pizza into or out of an oven. It transfers the pizza rather than providing the stationary baking surface.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A steel baking surface that stores heat and transfers it to dough in contact with it. Its heat transfer differs from a baking stone, so the two are not simply interchangeable materials.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A handled cutting wheel for dough or pastry. Plain and fluted edges produce different cut edges; the tool is distinct from a pastry blender that cuts fat into flour.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A tapered bag for dispensing soft mixtures such as icing, cream or mashed potato. A fitted tip can shape the output; piping is not limited to sweet decorations.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A spreading spatula whose blade is offset from the handle. The clearance helps spread icing or batter without the handle being in the same plane as the food.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A pasta-making tool that presses dough between rollers into sheets of adjustable thickness. A roller does not itself provide every cutting or extrusion function of a pasta machine.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A long, narrow grater with a rasp-like cutting surface, often used for fine citrus zest or hard cheese. Rasp describes the tool form; zest describes one use.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Equipment that removes air from compatible food packaging and closes or maintains its seal. Available modes and liquid handling vary by model; removing air alone does not establish safe storage conditions.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A cooking vessel with a shallow base and tall conical lid, associated with Moroccan cooking. The name also denotes dishes; this equipment identity is the vessel. Materials and heating compatibility vary.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A shallow cooking surface used in Mexican cooking for tortillas and toasting or roasting ingredients. Clay examples establish that the identity cannot be reduced to a metal griddle.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A shallow cooking surface used for foods such as flatbreads and dosa. Flat and slightly curved designs serve different tasks; the name does not imply one coating or heat-source compatibility.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Cut leaves into ribbons, commonly by stacking, rolling and slicing them. This leafy cut differs from making sticks from firm vegetables.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Cut very small, regular dice, commonly by cross-cutting julienned strips. It describes a deliberate cube shape rather than an irregular mince.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Cut vegetables into regular sticks thicker than julienne, as for crudités. Exact dimensions follow the recipe or teaching convention.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Trim vegetables into regular, curved oblong shapes. The classic seven-faced potato is one form, not a rule for every vegetable; this is not ordinary turning during cooking.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Prepare peeled, seeded tomato flesh in small pieces for a sauce or other dish. This scoped identity does not make every use of the broader French verb concasser tomato preparation.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Cut citrus segments free of their peel, white pith and enclosing membranes. This is more specific than dividing an unpeeled fruit into wedges.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Secure a bird with kitchen twine to hold its legs and wings close to the body for cooking. This entry concerns poultry preparation, not every act of tying.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Dispense a soft food mixture through a piping bag or tip to control its placement and shape. This includes savoury mixtures as well as icing.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution equivalence or broader aliases inferred.

improvements.added: A bench knife can portion a dough into pieces before shaping. The scraper name alone does not specify a cutting edge suitable for that job; choose the rigid bench form when portioning is the task.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A rasp form gives access to a small curved surface such as citrus peel. That access is a separate consideration from the size of its teeth; grater shape and the fineness of the result are not the same property.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A rasp-style zester can also grate hard cheese. This overlap explains why zesting tools appear among graters without making every grater a tool for removing only the outer citrus peel.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: The roller description above concerns the sheet-making form. A separate cutter determines noodle width; changing roller thickness does not change the width of a cutter. Extrusion machines are another form of pasta machine, not another setting on a sheet roller.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: End guides can limit the thickness of a dough sheet, but they do not guarantee a chosen diameter. If a dough portion reaches the guide thickness first, its final outline may remain smaller than the recipe requires.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Snipping herbs, cutting kitchen twine and shaping parchment are different uses of the same shears. A pull-apart joint aids access for cleaning, but it is a design feature to check rather than a property of every pair.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Deep grooves and excessive wear can make a board difficult to clean effectively. Cleaning routines do not remove that physical damage; USDA advises replacing worn boards with hard-to-clean grooves.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Separate usable vegetable trim from waste as you cut. Squaring food for regular cuts creates offcuts that may suit stock or sauce; a precise presentation need not mean discarding all the remaining edible material.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Peeling and trimming should remove the unwanted layer without taking an unnecessary amount of flesh. A short blade can work around small irregular areas; a large, tough rind calls for a different tool choice.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A support loop lets the illustrated strainer rest across a bowl while liquid drains. This support arrangement is separate from mesh fineness: both the opening size and how the sieve sits on the receiving vessel matter.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Rough chopping still benefits from reasonably similar piece sizes when the pieces will cook together. Irregular outlines and wildly different sizes are separate issues; a rustic cut need not mean uneven doneness.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Brunoise is a particular small, regular dice. The general instruction to dice does not automatically request brunoise, so preserve any size cue in the recipe rather than inferring the finest cut.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: For herbs, an initial coarse cut can be followed by repeated cuts to reach the intended fineness. Mincing does not require preserving the regular faces of a dice; its endpoint is the small-piece texture required by the dish.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Cross-cutting julienned strips produces brunoise. Batonnet stops at a thicker stick; these names distinguish the resulting shapes and sizes, not different knives that must be purchased.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Slicing can be an intermediate stage before sticks or dice. The first slices set one dimension of the later pieces, so inconsistent thickness at that stage carries through to the finished cut.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Fine grating can distribute hard cheese or citrus peel as small particles rather than visible strips. A tool capable of both tasks does not make their ingredients interchangeable; the recipe still determines what is being grated.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Zesting keeps the coloured peel, whereas supreming citrus keeps the flesh and removes peel and segment membranes. These preparations use different parts of the fruit and should not be treated as alternate names for peeling.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Folding pastry into layers during lamination is a different context from gently folding a foam mixture. A recipe must supply that context; repeated pastry folds are not an instruction to beat or stir a foam.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A dough docker repeats the puncturing action across a sheet. Its purpose differs from the continuous cut made by a pastry wheel: cutting the outline of a pastry piece does not dock its surface.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Rolling sets the dimensions of the sheet between folds. A pin with thickness guides controls one dimension, not the full rectangle, so check the required shape as well as thickness when building layers.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.
